clue.text: Native American's father turns up hurt

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
to ache is to hurt

explanation.surface: A Native American's father gets up from his seat in pain.
explanation.definitionFit: The Apache are a group of indigenous peoples of the American Southwest, so a member is a Native American.

clue.text: Reward for one getting on provides enjoyment

parts.note: the fruit of one's labours is its reward
Roman numeral one
taken as written

explanation.surface: A reward for someone advancing in life brings them pleasure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One getting on' reads as an ageing person, but it is just the numeral placed before the word on.
explanation.definitionFit: Fruition has an older sense of pleasurable possession or enjoyment, besides its usual sense of fulfilment.

clue.text: Guidance these days on sin

parts.note: AD (anno Domini) marks the present era
a vice is a sin

explanation.surface: Modern counselling about wrongdoing.
explanation.definitionFit: Advice is counsel or recommendation given to someone, which is guidance.

clue.text: Astute interpretation in law

indicators.note: an interpretation is a reading of something in a new way, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the word as printed, but the parse needs a third T that it does not have: the setter's slip

explanation.surface: A shrewd reading of the legislation.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder is a letter short: rearranging ASTUTE gives only six letters, and STATUTE needs a third T. The setter slipped.
explanation.definitionFit: A statute is a written law passed by a legislature.

clue.text: Composer about to jump in

parts.note: c is short for circa, about
to hop is to jump
taken as written

explanation.surface: A musician is ready to leap in and join.
explanation.definitionFit: Frédéric Chopin was a Polish composer of piano music, so he is an example of a composer.

clue.text: Paint English title over Latin

parts.note: standard abbreviation
a title is a name
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: Painting an English heading over a Latin one.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'over' means the first pieces sit above the last one.
explanation.definitionFit: Enamel is a glossy kind of paint that dries hard, so it can stand for paint.

clue.text: Goddess just atrophied away

indicators.note: something gone away has wandered off from its place, so the letters drift into another order

parts.note: taken as written as the anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A goddess simply wasted away.
explanation.definitionFit: Aphrodite is the Greek goddess of love and beauty.

clue.text: Name written in footwear that was well polished

indicators.note: something written in sits inside the item it is put into

parts.note: a shoe is an item of footwear
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: A name label inside a shoe that had been given a good shine.
explanation.definitionFit: Shone, past tense of shine, describes something that gleamed, as a well polished shoe does.

clue.text: Behave on rare visits to militants

parts.note: to act is to behave

indicators.note: rare can mean unusual or strange, so the letters appear in an odd order

parts.note: taken as written as the anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Advice on how to conduct yourself on the occasional visit to militants.
explanation.definitionFit: Activists campaign vigorously for a cause, which is what militants do.

clue.text: Emus returned, keeping quiet in the foam

indicators.note: returned means sent back the way it came, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
p is piano, quiet in music

explanation.surface: Some emus came back, quietly paddling through the foam.
explanation.definitionFit: Spume is froth or foam, especially that found on waves.

clue.text: Hello and goodbye, as Berlusconi might have put it

definitions.text: Hello and goodbye, as Berlusconi might have put it

parts.note: surface reading: a greeting and a farewell

parts.words: as Berlusconi might have put it
parts.note: setter's reading: Silvio Berlusconi was an Italian prime minister, so the word is Italian

explanation.walkthrough: One Italian word serves both for hello and for goodbye; the former Italian prime minister points to the language.
explanation.definitionFit: Ciao is the informal Italian greeting used both on meeting and on parting.

clue.text: Withdraw when about to grow weary

parts.note: re means about, concerning
to tire is to grow weary

explanation.surface: Pulling out of something just as fatigue is about to set in.
explanation.definitionFit: To retire is to withdraw, whether from work, a contest or a room.

clue.text: Shape altering mistakenly

indicators.note: done mistakenly, the letters land in the wrong places

parts.note: taken as written as the anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Changing a shape by error.
explanation.definitionFit: A triangle is a three-sided geometric figure, an example of a shape.

clue.text: Mild surprise expressed when geese leave the Home Counties behind

indicators.note: to leave a place is to go away from it, so those letters drop out of the word
left behind means abandoned, completing the instruction to drop letters

parts.note: taken as written
the Home Counties lie in the South East of England, abbreviated SE

explanation.surface: A little gasp as geese fly off from the countryside around London.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Counties are the English counties surrounding London, in the South East; drop those two letters from the end of geese.
explanation.definitionFit: Gee is an exclamation of mild surprise or enthusiasm.

clue.text: Juvenile creature left after pupil disappeared

indicators.note: something that has disappeared is no longer there, so it is taken out

parts.note: taken as written
L is for learner, a pupil

explanation.surface: A child was left behind after a schoolchild vanished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pupil' could be the eye's pupil, but here it is a learner, the L of a learner driver's plate.
explanation.definitionFit: An eft is a newt, especially a young one in its land-living stage, so a juvenile creature.

clue.text: Poetess pens erotica, partly for an old poet

indicators.note: partly means only a portion of the following words is used, a run of consecutive letters

parts.note: letters running across the end of the first word, all of the second and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A female poet writes erotica, some of it for a poet of old.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs from the last letter of Poetess through the start of erotica.
explanation.definitionFit: Edmund Spenser was the Elizabethan author of The Faerie Queene, an old poet.

clue.text: Second love on first sight — help!

parts.note: standard abbreviation
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

indicators.note: first asks for just the opening letter of the word that follows

parts.note: opening letter

explanation.surface: Falling in love again at first sight, with a cry for help.
explanation.definitionFit: SOS is the international distress signal, a call for help.

clue.text: For example, George is a nit!

parts.note: e.g. abbreviates for example
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: For instance, George is an idiot!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nit' looks like an insult for George, but it is the louse's egg.
explanation.definitionFit: A nit is the egg of a louse, so it is an example of the answer.

clue.text: It's about time to broadcast

indicators.note: about can mean turned round, so the word faces the other way

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: At last it is the moment to go on air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's about time' reads as an exasperated idiom, but 'about' turns round the word time.
explanation.definitionFit: To emit is to send out or give off, as a transmitter does with a signal.

clue.text: Study a hundred pet aberrations: it's an idea

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart

indicators.note: aberrations are departures from the normal, so the letters stray from their order

parts.note: Roman numeral for a hundred
taken as written as the anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Investigating a hundred cases of pets misbehaving is a notion.
explanation.definitionFit: A concept is an abstract idea or general notion.

clue.text: Dog on railway is mine

parts.note: a collie is a breed of dog
abbreviation for railway

explanation.surface: A dog on the train tracks is claimed as my own.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mine' looks like the possessive, but it is the noun for a pit.
explanation.definitionFit: A colliery is a coal mine together with its buildings.

clue.text: It's hard for unknown, quiet, egghead with daughter out of bed to be overexcited

parts.note: standard abbreviation, as on pencils
algebra uses x, y and z for unknowns
p is piano, quiet in music
read as egg-head: the head, or first letter, of egg
standard abbreviation
someone out of bed is up

explanation.surface: A strange tale of a quiet intellectual and his daughter, roused and agitated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Egghead' reads as an intellectual, but it splits into egg and an instruction to take its head.
explanation.definitionFit: Hyped up is an informal phrase for agitated or overstimulated, an idiom for overexcited.

clue.text: Judgment of story by Edinburgh, say

parts.note: a saga is a long story
Edinburgh is an example of a city

explanation.surface: An assessment of a tale written by someone from Edinburgh.
explanation.definitionFit: Sagacity is wisdom and sound judgment.

clue.text: More than one saw Proverbs

definitions.meaning: first meaning: several old sayings, a saw being a saying

explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' looks like the cutting tool or the past of see, but a saw is also an old saying.
explanation.definitionFit: Adages are traditional sayings, synonyms of both saws and proverbs.

clue.text: As a cub developed, you could count on it

indicators.note: something developed has grown into a new form, so the letters take a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: As a young cub grew up, you could rely on it.
explanation.definitionFit: An abacus is a frame of beads on rods used for counting, so you literally count on it.

clue.text: House for student down with depression

parts.note: HO is an abbreviation for house
L for learner
feeling down is feeling low

explanation.surface: Student housing comes with low spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Down' and 'depression' both suggest mood, but depression is a dip in the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A hollow is a sunken area or dip in a surface, a depression.

clue.text: Get better, reaching the endless state of well-being

indicators.note: endless means without its end, so the final letter is cut

parts.note: to heal is to get better
taken as written

explanation.surface: Recovering until you reach the infinite condition of feeling well.
explanation.definitionFit: Health is the state of being free from illness, physical well-being.

clue.text: Brass decoration for gold on doctor's large uniform

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry
MO is a medical officer
standard abbreviation, as on clothing sizes
U is uniform in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: Brass trim instead of gold on a doctor's big uniform.
explanation.definitionFit: Ormolu is gilded bronze or a gold-coloured brass alloy used for ornamental fittings on furniture.

clue.text: Some urban allegories are hackneyed

indicators.note: some means only part of the words that follow is used

parts.note: letters spanning the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: A literary judgement that some city fables are clichéd.
explanation.definitionFit: Banal means trite and unoriginal, the same as hackneyed.

clue.text: Lawyers' jargon involving narrow interpretations of the rules

definitions.meaning: first meaning: legal terms and expressions
second meaning: strict adherence to the letter of the law

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as one description, but each half is a separate sense of the same plural noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Legalisms are both legal terms of art and instances of excessively literal rule-following.

clue.text: Kind of information we go after

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
us is the object form of we

explanation.surface: We chase a certain sort of information.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kind of' looks like part of a phrase, but Kind alone is the definition; gen is informal British for information.
explanation.definitionFit: A genus is a class or category, a kind, as in biological classification.

clue.text: Insect seen in goat race?

parts.note: a goat is a butter, an animal that butts
to fly is to rush or race

explanation.surface: An insect spotted at a goat race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goat race' sounds like a country fair event, but a goat butts, so it is a butter, and to race is to fly.
explanation.definitionFit: A butterfly is a winged insect with large coloured wings.
